name: MedVIGIL
description: MedVIGIL tests whether medical vision-language models recognise when the evidence for an answer has failed. Each vision-required radiology question is posed with intact evidence and then with a false premise, a paraphrase, a negation, a specificity drop, a knowledge-only rewrite, or an ROI-masked, ROI-only or left-right-flipped image; a fluent non-refusal answer under broken evidence is a silent failure. This public release holds 240 cases (VQA-RAD 120, SLAKE 60, ROCO 60), 2,002 five-option MCQ probes with open-ended twins and 180 counterfactual triplets. The full benchmark adds 60 chest-radiograph cases from MIMIC-CXR and CheXpert (554 probes), which are available only to credentialed users (CXR_ACCESS.md).
citeAs: @inproceedings{jiang2026medvigil, title={{MedVIGIL}: Evaluating Trustworthy Medical {VLMs} Under Broken Visual Evidence}, author={Jiang, Hanqi and Chen, Junhao and Pan, Yi and Chen, Lifeng and You, Weihang and Gong, Haozhen and Yan, Ruiyu and Lv, Jinglei and Zhao, Lin and Ren, Hui and Li, Quanzheng and Liu, Tianming and Li, Xiang}, booktitle={Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS), Evaluations and Datasets Track}, year={2026}}
rai:dataCollection: Cases were sampled with stratified quotas over five clinical risk tiers from public medical VQA and caption collections: VQA-RAD (120), SLAKE (60) and ROCO (60) in this release, plus 60 chest radiographs from MIMIC-CXR and CheXpert in the credentialed arm. Each case was then annotated by board-certified radiologists as described in rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images, questions and answers from VQA-RAD and SLAKE and images with captions from ROCO, used under their licences. No new patient data were collected.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: text_only_answerable is empty for 55 VQA-RAD cases. 90 cases have a whole-image ROI box and therefore no ROI-masked or ROI-only probe. A probe family is absent for a case when no clinically valid rewrite exists (for example the negation of a modality question). Triplets exist for the 180 cases whose golds satisfy all three triplet invariants. The 60 credentialed chest-radiograph cases are withheld from this release.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Source cases were deduplicated by pixel hash and balanced across sources and risk tiers.

ROI boxes are clamped to the image. ROI-masked images fill the box with RGB (128, 128, 128); ROI-only images fill its complement; lr_flip mirrors the image. Cases whose box covers the whole image get no ROI variants.
Every probe is wrapped in five options A-E; option E is the probe-specific safe action, and image-variant probes reuse the option set of their case's text probe.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Stage 1, screening: radiologists R1 and R2 keep a source question only if it needs the image and its wording does not give the answer away. Stage 2, annotation: R1 and R2 independently annotate the clinical risk tier, text-only answerability, gold answer, five-option candidate set with its refusal option, ROI box and laterality flag; GPT-5.5 drafts the paraphrase, negation, specificity-drop and knowledge-only rewrites, two false-premise traps per case and the V-CF condition of each triplet, and R1 and R2 review and edit every draft. Stage 3, consolidation: radiologist P3 adjudicates every disagreement, finalises every released field and drops any perturbation that violates a construction invariant (paraphrase keeps the gold, negation inverts it, knowledge-only needs no image, a trap contradicts the image, ROI masking removes the answer-relevant region, triplet golds satisfy anchor = T-CF != V-CF). Full field definitions: PIPELINE.md.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each case-level label was annotated independently by R1 and R2; every disagreement was adjudicated by P3. Inter-annotator agreement is reported in the accompanying paper.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Two independent radiologist annotations per case (R1, R2), adjudicated and finalised by a third radiologist (P3).
rai:annotatorDemographics: Three board-certified radiologists affiliated with Massachusetts General Hospital and Harvard Medical School: two thoracic subspecialists with 6 and 3 years of post-residency experience (R1, R2) and one cardiovascular subspecialist with 10 years (P3).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-5.5 (OpenAI): drafted the paraphrase, negation, specificity-drop and knowledge-only rewrites, the two false-premise traps per case and the V-CF conditions; every draft was reviewed and edited by R1 and R2 and finalised by P3.
Python Imaging Library: deterministic rendering of the ROI-masked, ROI-only and left-right-flipped images.
rai:dataUseCases: Construct: evidence-conditional safe failure of medical vision-language models, that is, whether a model withholds an answer (option E) when the evidence has been broken by a false premise or by removing the answer-relevant region, while still answering intact, paraphrased, negated and specificity-reduced questions. Validity rests on paired probes that hold the case fixed and change one evidence channel: original probes control for capability so blanket refusal cannot score as safety, ROI-only versus ROI-masked probes separate region-grounded from prior-driven answers, and knowledge-only probes bound language-prior answering. Intended for evaluation only; not for training or clinical use.
rai:dataBiases: Selection: cases come from four public English-language radiology collections, so modalities, body regions and finding prevalence follow those sources rather than clinical practice, and this release contains no chest-radiograph cases. Label position: option order is fixed; the gold is option A for every answerable probe except 27 laterality-dependent flips (B-D), and option E for every trap and ROI-masked probe, so a model with a positional preference is advantaged unless options A-D are permuted. Pretraining overlap: the public sources may appear in model training data. Annotators: three radiologists, two of them thoracic subspecialists.
rai:dataLimitations: 240 public cases (300 with the credentialed arm) support falsifying safe-failure claims, not fine-grained subgroup analysis. English only and radiology only. ROI boxes are rectangles for placing masks, not segmentation labels. V-CF conditions are textual, not regenerated images. Full-image acquisition artefacts and severity-aware metrics are not covered. Not a clinical tool.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive: exposes medical VLMs that answer confidently through broken evidence before deployment, and weights those failures by clinical risk. Negative: a high score does not certify clinical safety; scores may be inflated by pretraining overlap with public sources; and tuning to the probes could improve the benchmark score without improving grounding. The data must not be used for clinical decision-making.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Health or medical data: de-identified medical images from public research collections. No names, dates, contact details or other direct identifiers, and no demographic attributes are recorded. Credentialed chest radiographs (MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert) and their reports are not redistributed.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Case identifiers are immutable. Corrections ship as new revisions of the Hugging Face repository with a changelog entry; earlier revisions stay addressable by commit. Issues: https://github.com/hq0709/MedVIGIL/issues. Planned: fresh cases beyond legacy public sources, more specialties, severity-aware metrics.
